extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and working creative writers (fiction, poetry, memoir) seeking craft, publication, and career advice
extracted.subtask_description: A Writer's Digest 'What's New' index page linking to short posts and resources offering guidance on craft, submission materials, agents' tastes, revision, platform-building, prompts, and writer career strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make time to write / prioritize writing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stop trying to find time to write. Instead, make time." Identify the time of day when you are most creative, then claim that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show up at the page. Get up early if you have to. Lock a door if you have to. Turn off your phone and Internet. Whatever it takes for you to carve out your time—do it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe poetic form constraints (sijo)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sijo poetic form is only three lines long but packs a lot into those lines; it's more lyrical than a haiku.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing sijo be aware of the three-line structure and the density of content expected in that short form (useful as an example of respecting form-specific rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Match submissions to agents' stated interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents describe clearly what they're seeking; submit work that fits their genres/themes (e.g., 'Young adult and middle grade (especially contemporary for both), romance, new adult, contemporary women's fiction, sci-fi, fantasy, and erotica' — Laura Zats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read agent alerts carefully and target submissions to their lists (example: Nikki Terpilowski seeks women's fiction, southern fiction, multicultural literary fiction, upmarket African-American fiction, steam funk, romance (all kinds except category...), graphic novels, Manga, YA, MG, children's picture books, time travel, reincarnation, mythology, ancient civilizations, magical and animist realism, Japan, American history, military/espionage, narrative nonfiction about food/beverage, travel/expat life, international relations, prescriptive nonfiction on spirituality/parenting/health).

rubrics_metrics.name: Build and maintain an author platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Having an effective writer platform is necessary to sell more books and increase a book's discoverability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform tactics include blogging, public speaking, and other visibility-building activities; platform matters whether traditionally published or self-published and contributes to launch success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise manuscript to professional submission-readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Art of Revision: Perfecting Your Book For Submission" — agents/editors look for a polished manuscript and will ask: Is grammar all that important, or should the story speak for itself? How many revisions should a manuscript go through before it's considered 'ready'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to do multiple revisions, cut and streamline word count, and prioritize story clarity and craft alongside grammar. Submit polished material for agent/editor critique (e.g., synopsis or opening pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek objective, knowledgeable critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rely only on enthusiastic friends/family; get an objective critique from someone reasonably knowledgeable about your genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join or form a writing group. Accept 100% open, honest comments even if they sting — they are invaluable for improving quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare strong submission materials: query, synopsis, opening pages
rubrics_metrics.description: When submission materials arrive they land among hundreds; agents make requests from the few letters that impress them. Learn to write a dynamite query letter, a one-page synopsis, and dynamite first pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamline submission materials to stand out. Workshops/boot camps and agent critiques can help you craft these elements. Etiquette in dealing with agents and an author platform also matter alongside manuscript basics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance effort in submissions (not too much, not too little)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who get rejected tend to fall into one of two categories when submitting materials: they try too hard, or not enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for concise, compelling materials that neither oversell nor undersell the work; learn what constitutes appropriate polish and presentation for your target market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure memoir with truthful, universal resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must build a shelter with our truth." Memoir should offer a structure that allows other people to 'shelter' there — make the story useful and meaningful to readers rather than self-indulgent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on shaping truth into a form that illuminates broader human experience; consider which elements to include or trim so readers can connect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use short, regular exercises to maintain productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: A '12-Day Plan of Simple Writing Exercises' can restart your engine and help you keep writing without eating up too much time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily or short-duration exercises build habit and can produce material worth refining; useful when returning to writing or combating writer's block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare practically for conferences and pitches
rubrics_metrics.description: Before attending a writer's conference, plan logistics (what to wear, what to bring) and prepare pitches — it's normal to feel nervous beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring materials for scheduled pitches; plan wardrobe suitable for the event and the meetings you booked; advance preparation reduces panic and increases confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build writer relationships and networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain friendships with writers whose work and personality you value; a network of good writers who are also good people will advance your career and enrich your life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer feedback, share submission calls and job postings, celebrate victories, and support each other — professional relationships can lead to collaborations and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to meet traditional-publication standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional critique services evaluate submissions to point out reasons work may be getting rejected or may not meet the standards of traditional publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pursuing traditional publication, ensure manuscript polish, appropriate length/word count, clear voice, and market fit; consider paid/professional feedback if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted learning opportunities (webinars, boot camps) for concrete skill-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Webinars and boot camps (e.g., 'Create Your Writer Platform', 'The Anatomy of a Query Letter', 'Agent One-on-One Boot Camp') teach specific, actionable skills like query writing, creating a one-page synopsis, crafting opening pages, and platform-building.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage instructor critiques and opportunities to submit sample pages for feedback; such focused instruction can lead to direct improvements and, sometimes, agent signings.
